Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:10:1.hebrew: הנשמע בדבר אביו למקום - אם מכיר באנשי המקום שמכבדים אביו, לחלוק לו כבוד לקבל דברים שיאמר בשמו — אל יתלה הכבוד בעצמו, ואפי' יודע שיכבדוהו כאביו, אלא יתלה הכבוד באביו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:10:1.english: One who is heeded in the matter of his father [sent] to a place - If he knows that the people of that place respect his father, [and are disposed] to accord him honor [by] accepting the things he will say in his name, he must not attribute the honor to himself, even if he knows that they would honor him like his father; rather, he should attribute the honor to his father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:10:2.hebrew: שלחוני בשביל אבא - שהוא צריך לי. אבל אם אינו נשמע למקום בדבר אביו כדבר עצמו, אל יתלה באביו, שאינו לו אלא גנאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:10:2.english: Send me on Father’s behalf - [Meaning,] that he needs me. But if he is not heeded in that place in the matter of his father as [much as] in his own matter, he should not attribute [it] to his father, for it is only a disgrace to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:11:1.english: May I be an atonement for his resting [place] - May all evil that is destined to come upon his soul come upon me.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:11:2.hebrew: מכאן ואילך - כבר קבל מה שקבל, שאין משפט רשעי ישראל בגיהנם אלא י"ב חדש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:11:2.english: From this time onward - He has already received whatever [punishment] he was to receive, for the judgment of the wicked of Israel in Gehinnom is only twelve months.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:12:1.hebrew: חכם משנה שם אביו כו' - חכם הדורש דרשה ברבים, ולוחש לתורגמן והוא משמיע — משנה שם אביו ושם רבו. אם בא לומר דבר הלכה שאמר אביו או רבו, לוחש לתורגמן: "כך אמר אבא מורי", "כך אמר רבי ומורי":
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:12:1.english: A Sage changes the name of his father, etc. - A Sage who delivers a lecture in public, and whispers to the disseminator and he announces [it] — changes the name of his father and the name of his teacher. If he comes to state a matter of Halakhah that his father or his teacher said, he whispers to the disseminator: "Thus said my father, my teacher," [or] "Thus said my master and teacher."

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:12:2.hebrew: אבל התורגמן - המשמיע לרבים אינו משנה, אלא מכנהו בשמו ואומר: "כך אמר פלוני":
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:12:2.english: But the disseminator - The one who announces [it] to the public does not change [the name], but rather refers to him by his name and says: "Thus said So-and-so."

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:12:3.english: Whose father? - [This refers to the statement that] the disseminator does not alter [the wording].

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:12:4.hebrew: אי נימא אבוה דתורגמן - אם לוחש לו חכם דבר הלכה בשם אביו של תורגמן להשמיע לרבים בשם אומרו, לא ישנה לומר "כך אמר אבא מורי", אלא קורהו בשמו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:12:4.english: If we say [it means] the father of the disseminator - If a Sage whispers a halakhic matter to him in the name of the disseminator's father, to make [it] heard to the public in the name of the one who said it, [the disseminator] should not change [it] to say, "Thus said my father, my teacher," but rather he calls him by his name.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:12:5.english: Is that to say the disseminator is not obligated - [Is] he [not obligated] to honor his father?

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:13:1.hebrew: כי הוה דרש בפירקא - ולוחש דבר הלכה לתורגמן בשם רב אשי אביו, איהו אמר לתורגמן: "כך אמר אבא מורי":
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:13:1.english: When he would expound at the public lecture - And [when] whispering a matter of Halakhah to the interpreter in the name of Rav Ashi, his father, he would say to the interpreter: "Thus said my father, my teacher."

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:13:2.hebrew: ואמוריה - כשהוא משמיע לרבים בשם אומרו, אומר: "כך אמר רב אשי", ואינו אומר: "כך אמר אביו ואדוניו של חכם":
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:13:2.english: And his disseminator - When he makes [it] heard to the public in the name of the one who said it, he says: “So said Rav Ashi,” and does not say: “So said the father and master of the Sage.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:14:1.english: [One] does not stand in his place - In the place designated for his father to stand there in the council of elders with his colleagues in counsel.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:14:2.hebrew: ולא מכריעו - אם היה אביו וחכם אחר חלוקין בדבר הלכה, לא יאמר: ״נראים דברי פלוני״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:14:2.english: And he may not choose sides - If his father and another Sage were in disagreement regarding a matter of halakhah, he may not say: "The words of so-and-so appear [correct]."

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:1:1.hebrew: ומביאו לעוה"ב - שמכבדו בדברו דברים טובים ונחומים, והמלאכה מטיל עליו בלשון רכה — מראה לו צורך השעה, שאינן יכולין להתפרנס אלא ביגיעה זו. ובגמרת ירושלמי גרס: מעשה בשניהם. מעשה באחד שהיה מאכיל לאביו פסיוני. פעם אחת אמר לו אביו: "מאין לך כל אלה?" אמר לו: "סבא, מה איכפת לך? טחון ואכול!" — כלומר, לעוס ואכול; הראהו שקשה לו. ושוב מעשה באחד שהיה טוחן בריחיים, והיה לו אב זקן, ושלח המלך בשביל אביו לבא לעבודת המלך. אמר לו בנו: "אבא, טחון, ואני אלך תחתיך לעבודת המלך שאין לה קצבה":
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:1:1.english: And brings him to the World-to-Come - In that he honors him by speaking good and comforting words to him, and he imposes the work upon him with gentle speech, showing him the need of the hour — that they cannot sustain themselves except through this toil. And in the Yerushalmi Gemara, the text reads an incident regarding both of them: An incident concerning one who would feed his father pheasants: Once, his father said to him, "From where do you have all these?" He said to him, "Old man, what do you care? Grind and eat!" — that is to say, chew and eat; he showed him that it was burdensome to him. And another incident concerning one who was grinding with a millstone, and he had an elderly father, and the king sent for his father to come for the king's labor. His son said to him, "Father, grind, and I will go in your place to the king's labor, which has no fixed limit."

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:2:1.hebrew: חמשה בני סמכי הוה ליה לאבימי בחיי אביו - ואפילו הכי, כי הוה קרי ר' אבהו אבבא, היה אבימי רץ ופותח לו, ואינו מניח לאחד מבניו לילך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:2:1.english: Avimi had five ordained sons during his father’s lifetime - And even so, when Rabbi Abbahu called at the gate, Avimi would run and open [it] for him, and would not let one of his sons go.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:2:2.english: Yes, yes - I will open [it], I will open [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:3:1.hebrew: איסתייעא מילתא - בעודו גחין לפניו, שהבין במדרש מזמור אחד שבספר תהלים, שלא היה מבין בו קודם לכן לדורשו. וי"מ, שמקרא זה לבדו דרש: ״מזמור לאסף, אלהים באו גוים בנחלתך״ וגו׳ — ״קינה לאסף״ מיבעי ליה?! ודרש כך: שאמר אסף שירה על שכילה הקב"ה חמתו בעצים ואבנים שבביתו, ומתוך כך הותיר פליטה בישראל, שאלמלא כך, לא נשתייר משונאי ישראל שריד. וכן הוא אומר: ״כלה ה' את חמתו ויצת אש בציון״ (איכה ד׳:י״א):
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:3:1.english: He was aided [by Heaven] - While he was [still] bent over before him — in that he understood the homiletical interpretation of a psalm in the Book of Psalms that he had not understood beforehand [how] to expound. And some explain that he expounded this verse alone: “A psalm of Asaph: O God, the nations have come into Your inheritance...” (Psalms 79:1) — it should have [stated], “A lament of Asaph”! And he expounded [it] thus: That Asaph uttered song because the Holy One, blessed be He, spent His wrath upon the wood and stones of His House, and thereby left a remnant in Israel; for had it not been so, not a single remnant would have remained of the enemies of Israel [a euphemism for Israel itself]. And so it says: “The Lord has spent His fury... and He kindled a fire in Zion” (Lamentations 4:11).

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:4:1.hebrew: כגון אנא - שאני אהוב לאבי ויקיר לאמי, ועושין לי זאת — מה אעשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:4:1.english: [One] such as I - For I am beloved to my father and precious to my mother, and they do this for me — what should I do?

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:4:2.english: Since he is a Torah scholar, he will be disheartened - If you accept service from him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:6:1.hebrew: אשרי מי שלא חמאן - שאי אפשר לקיים כבודם ככל הצורך, והוא נענש עליהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:6:1.english: Fortunate is one who never saw them - For it is impossible to fulfill their honor to the full extent required, and he is punished on their account.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:8:1.english: You are determined to leave - [Rabbi Yoḥanan] thought that his intention was to return to his place, to Babylonia.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:8:2.english: [May the Omnipresent] return you in peace - To your place.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:9:1.hebrew: אמר ליה - ר' אסי לר"א: דלמא, ח"ו, מרתח רתח עלי רבי יוחנן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31b:9:1.english: He said to him - Rav Asi [said] to Rabbi Elazar: Perhaps, God forbid, Rabbi Yochanan was angry with me?

Tosafot on Kiddushin 31b:3:1.hebrew: איסתייא מילתא - בעודו גחין לפניו, שהבין ודרש "מזמור לאסף, אלהים באו גוים בנחלתך", שלא היה מבין בו מקודם לכן, ודרשו. וי"מ שמקרא זה לבד דרש: "מזמור לאסף" — "קינה לאסף" מיבעי' ליה! ודרש שאמר אסף שירה על שכילה הקב"ה חמתו על העצים ועל האבנים שבביתו, ומתוך כך הותיר פליטה מישראל, שאלמלא כך לא נשתייר משונאי ישראל שריד ופליט; וכן הוא אומר: "כלה ה' את חמתו ויצת אש בציון". כך פירש בקונטרס. אך יש במדרש שאסף אמר שירה על שטבעו בארץ שעריה. משל לשפחה שהלכה לשאוב מים מן הבאר ונפל כדה לבאר, והיתה מצטערת ובוכה, עד שבאתה שפחת המלך לשאוב ובידה כלי של זהב ונפל אותו כלי שם; התחילה הראשונה לשורר, ואמרה: "עד עכשיו לא הייתי סבורה שיוציא שום אדם כדי, שהוא של חרס, מן הבאר, שאינו נחשב; ועכשיו, מי שיוציא אותו של זהב יוציא כדי עמו!" כך בני קרח שהיו בלועים, כשראו שטבעו בארץ שעריה, אמרו שירה; אמרו: "מי שיוציא השערים יוציא גם אותנו!" לכך אמר אסף מזמור, שהוא ממשפחת קרח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 31b:3:1.english: He was aided in the matter - [This occurred] while he was bent over before him, as he understood and expounded [the psalm], “A psalm of Asaph: O God, the nations have entered into Your inheritance” (Psalms 79:1), which he had not understood beforehand and [now] expounded. And some explain that he expounded this verse alone: “A psalm of Asaph” — it should have [said], “A lamentation of Asaph”! And he expounded that Asaph recited a song because the Holy One, Blessed be He, vented His wrath upon the wood and upon the stones of His House, and thereby spared a remnant of Israel; for had it not been so, there would not have remained of the enemies of Israel [a euphemism for Israel itself] a remnant or survivor. And so it says: “The Lord has spent His fury... and kindled a fire in Zion” (Lamentations 4:11). So explained the Kuntres [Rashi]. However, it is [found] in the Midrash that Asaph recited a song over [the fact] that “Her gates sank into the ground” (Lamentations 2:9). [This is] a parable of a maidservant who went to draw water from the well, and her pitcher fell into the well, and she was grieved and weeping, until the king’s maidservant came to draw [water] with a golden vessel in her hand, and that vessel fell in there. The first [maidservant] began to sing and said: “Until now, I did not believe that anyone would retrieve my pitcher from the well, since it is of earthenware, which is of no account; but now, whoever retrieves that [vessel] of gold will retrieve my pitcher along with it!” So too, the sons of Korah, who were swallowed up [in the earth], when they saw that “Her gates sank into the ground,” recited a song. They said: “Whoever brings out the gates will bring us out as well!” Therefore Asaph said “A psalm,” as he was from the family of Korah.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 31b:5:1.hebrew: ר' טרפון הויא ליה אמא - יש בירושלמי: פעם אחת אמיה דר' טרפון אבדה פזמקי דידה בחצירה, ויצאתה ממטתה לבקשו, ושם ר' טרפון ידו תחת רגליה על הקרקע שלא תטנף רגליה, והיתה דורסת על ידיו. ועוד איתא בירושלמי, דאמיה דר' ישמעאל: כל שעתא ושעתא דהוה אתי רבי ישמעאל מבי מדרשא, היתה רוחצת את רגליו והיתה שותה את המים. כששמע רבי ישמעאל שהיתה עושה כך, היה מסרב בדבר; עד שבאת לפני חכמים, והיתה קובלת על ר' ישמעאל בנה שלא היה מקיים מצות כיבוד. ונבהלו חכמים בדבר, ושאלו לרבי ישמעאל, וספר להם המעשה, וצוו לו שיניחנה לעשות רצונה, ובענין זה הוא כיבוד:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 31b:5:1.english: "Rabbi Tarfon had a mother" - It is [stated] in the Yerushalmi: Once, the mother of Rabbi Tarfon lost her slipper in her courtyard, and she went out from her bed to search for it, and Rabbi Tarfon placed his hand under her feet upon the ground so that her feet would not get soiled, and she stepped on his hands. And it is further stated in the Yerushalmi that the mother of Rabbi Yishmael, each and every time that Rabbi Yishmael would come from the study hall, would wash his feet and drink the water. When Rabbi Yishmael heard that she was doing so, he would resist the matter, until she came before the Sages and complained about Rabbi Yishmael, her son, that he was not fulfilling the mitzvah of honoring [parents]. And the Sages were alarmed by the matter, and they asked Rabbi Yishmael, and he recounted the incident to them. And they commanded him to allow her to do her will, and [that] in this manner is [fulfillment of] honor.
